features: ⚠️ THIS RELEASE DOES NOT TOUCH THE DATABASE, but it changes what comes out printed: reprinting an allocation you already issued gives the same totals as before, with the prior balance in a different column. That is the point of this release, and it belongs before everything else.

THE COLUMN THAT NO LONGER MATCHED WHAT WAS APPROVED — A building manager imported his own building, drew up a budget with a single item (management fee, € 1,000.00) allocated on a single thousandths table, and printed the allocation: that column came to € 1,214.36. One owner's share, € 1,277.35, was higher than the total of the column it sat in. Then he looked at the instalment schedule and stopped: «this is where I get stuck, no point going on». He was right, and he had reached the cause without seeing the code.

WHY IT SWELLED. The allocation's row totals add up every instalment in the plan, including instalment zero which carries the opening balances; the column cells, instead, are rebuilt from the expense headings' budget alone. The difference — a «remainder» which is, by construction, that person's prior balance — was being dropped onto whichever table that owner weighs most in. With a single table, it took the lot. On his data the arithmetic closes to the cent: the four ceased holders came to € 271.23, the current owners to € 485.59, and the difference is exactly the € 214.36 too many. A ceased holder's balance goes jointly onto the unit under art. 63 disp. att. c.c., so it has no thousandths-bearing person and was already in the right column; a current owner's balance was not. The defect fired because there were mid-year ownership changes: without them it would never have shown.

THE FIX: ONE ROUTE, NOT TWO. The prior balance always goes to the «direct charge» column. This isn't a new rule — it is the one already applied to anyone with no weight in any table, with the right reasoning written beside it: a prior balance belongs to no thousandths table, and that is precisely what the column means. The allocation declares two guarantees, that every column adds up to its headings' budget and that every row matches what was actually charged: the old mechanism saved the second by breaking the first. Now they coexist.

THE CREDITS THAT VANISHED FROM THE CELLS. In the printouts a cell showed the amount only if it was positive, while the column and row totals added the real value, negatives included: on every row of someone in credit, the table did not add up across. On screen the same figure read correctly, so the program gave two different answers to the same number. The example that found it: an owner with € 203.72 of credit in instalment zero and € 51.91 to pay in the first; the instalment-zero cell was blank and the row total printed € -151.81 — correct, and impossible to check by hand. Fixed in four documents: the instalment schedule, allocation by table, allocation by heading, and expense allocation. Zero still prints a dash, because it means «does not take part»; a negative now prints.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW. The sign filter dates from 1.9.1, the allocation's realignment from 1.10.0-beta.8: neither was born with the data import. But an import brings in opening balances and ceased holders in one go — exactly the conditions that set them off. It is the price of a feature that puts the program in front of real data: the defects that were already there become reachable. The importer itself got nothing wrong — the € 4,065.31 in instalment zero is the exact sum of the «final balance» column of the source file, 27 rows, not a cent lost.
